title: Spinlings: a Claude-built creature game that lives above the coding prompt
author: Other-Income-5085
selftext:
I built Spinlings, a free, open-source creature game inside Claude Code. You collect a three-card team, trade cards with other players, and duel their saved teams while Claude works.

The original version was built with Claude: a TypeScript creature and battle engine, TSX views for the prompt band and collection pane, and a Cloudflare Worker/D1 backend. The offline client and online server use the same battle rules. Codex helped with the later UI and test iterations.

The interesting design constraint is attention. This sits next to real coding work, so a duel should still make sense if you look away. Teams fight automatically; there is an optional timed special action if you want to intervene. Opponents are saved teams, so you do not have to arrange a live match.

The actual UI work was messier than the first concepts. Artwork clicks behaved differently from text in Desktop, and layouts that looked fine in a large pane became cramped in small ones. Getting the card click targets and team-slot picker right took several iterations.

The game makes no model calls and does not read prompts, replies or project files. Creature sprites are generated from pixel parts and seeds. It requires Claude Code 2.1.287+ or a compatible Desktop Code session.

I would like feedback on the attention tradeoff: would you use the optional special action, or mostly let your team fight?

[Source, screenshots and install instructions](https://github.com/416rehman/spinlings) (MIT).
